== Biography ==
The inscription found in Crawford Old Churchyard and Leadhills Cemetery in Crawford, Lanarkshire, Scotland, commemorates various members of the Glasgow family. Specifically, the inscription pays tribute to William Glasgow, who served as a gamekeeper to the Right Honourable Earl of Hopetoun, noting his passing on April 26, 1853, at the age of 74. Additionally, the inscription memorializes his wife, Janet Thomson, who passed away on April 1, 1845, at the age of 62. The inscription also mentions three of their children: John and James, who died in infancy, and George, who passed away at the age of 7 on July 21, 1816. Lastly, the inscription remembers Isabel Glasgow, who passed away on November 27, 1881, at the age of 73. This commemorative inscription is documented within the Scotland Monumental Inscriptions collection, a subset of the Birth, Marriage, Death & Parish Records category. It provides insights into the lives and familial connections of those interred in the Crawford Old Churchyard and Leadhills Cemetery, contributing to the historical records of the area.

== Research Notes ==
=== Possible William Allen Glasgow, Royal Engineers commission, 1795 ===
Gentleman Cadet William Allen Glasgow is announced as second lieutenant in the Corps of Royal Engineers, vice Lefebvre, promoted, dated 1 October 1795.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/395720951/ The Caledonian Mercury, 1795-10-15, p.4].</ref>

The commission date is 1 October 1795, not the 15 October publication day. "Gentleman Cadet" describes his prior status; the notice gives no parents, birthplace or subsequent career. A William without a recorded middle name remains a possible identification.

This may concern [[Glasgow-2715]]. Estimated c. 1779 Crawford birth is compatible with a young cadet. Estimated age and a missing middle name do not exclude him; no engineering-service connection.
